Front Range Pool League

Trap ’Em

An 8-Ball game of offense & defense

Every shot is offense. Every shot is defense.

Trap ’Em is a strategic variation of 8-Ball where every player gets exactly ONE shot per turn at the table.
You’re not just trying to pocket your own ball — you’re trying to play safe against your opponent.

How to play

Played under the current CSI Official Rules for 8-Ball, with a few Trap ’Em specific rules:

Each player gets exactly ONE shot per turn at the table, regardless of the result of that shot.

The one exception: a ball legally pocketed on the break earns the breaker one more shot.

Pocket a legal ball?Your turn is over.
Miss?Your turn is over.
Play a safety?Your turn is over.
Scratch?Your turn is over, and your opponent gets ball in hand.
Bad hit or no rail?Your turn is over. Your opponent may shoot it as it lies or make you shoot again.

Players alternate one shot at a time until the game is won.

Rules

1The break

If the breaker legally pockets a ball on the break, they get one more shot to try to establish their group.
After that shot, the turn passes. If nothing is pocketed, the turn passes right away.

2After the break

The table is open. To claim a group, call the ball and pocket it legally.
A ball that drops without a call does not set the groups, and the table stays open.

38-ball on the break

Handled the same as CSI 8-Ball.

4When to call your shot

Only two shots need a call: any shot at the 8-ball, and a shot on an open table that you want to set your group.
Pocketing the 8 without calling it, or in a pocket you didn’t call, loses the game.
Once groups are set, no other calls are needed except for the 8-ball.

5Ball in hand only on a scratch

Ball in hand is given only when the cue ball is scratched. Ball in hand does not add an extra shot.

6Bad hit or no rail: opponent’s option

If the shooter fails to hit a ball of their own group first, or no ball reaches a rail after contact, it is a foul but not ball in hand.
The opponent may shoot the table as it lies, or make the shooter shoot again from where the balls stopped.
That shot is the shooter’s one shot, and then the turn passes as normal.
On an open table, any ball except the 8 counts as the shooter’s group.

7Pocketing your opponent’s ball

On a legal shot it is not a foul. The ball stays down, and your turn is over like any other shot.

8Stalemate

If neither player can make progress, the CSI stalemate rule applies: re-rack, and the original breaker breaks again.

The strategy

In regular 8-Ball, making a ball lets you keep shooting, so position play is about leaving yourself a shot.
In Trap ’Em, your opponent comes to the table after every shot.

Can I make my ball?

Can I make my ball and leave my opponent trapped?

  • Pocket a ball while hiding the cue ball.
  • Use your remaining balls as blockers.
  • Tie up your opponent’s balls.
  • Avoid opening their problem areas.
  • Sometimes the best ball to make isn’t the easiest one.
  • Sometimes a ball is worth more on the table than in a pocket.

Winning the game

Same as standard 8-Ball: legally pocket your group, then legally pocket the 8-ball.

All normal CSI 8-Ball rules still apply unless changed by the Trap ’Em rules above:

The break Open table Establishing groups Legal shots Fouls Ball in hand The 8-ball Loss of game
